title: Docs
subtitle: Setup, conventions, the i18n contract, and the update workflow.

intro.title: What AureCook is
intro.body: An internal shadcn registry. Declare it once in components.json, then install components with the CLI — the source lands in your repo, with no package in between to wait on for releases.

install.title: Setup
install.step1: Declare the public registry in your repo's components.json:
install.step2: Install your first item. The CLI pulls both registry and npm dependencies:
install.step3: Done. Files land in your repo's own alias directories, not AureCook's.

internal.title: Private registry
internal.body: Internal items live in their own namespace and need a token. Put AURECOOK_TOKEN in your shell or CI environment — never commit it.

i18n.title: The i18n contract
i18n.body: A registry component must never require the consuming repo to have a dictionary. User-facing strings resolve through three tiers, highest priority first.
i18n.tier1: A labels prop from the call site — wins over everything.
i18n.tier2: A localization object passed to the root component — translates a whole cluster at once.
i18n.tier3: English defaults baked into the item — it runs in a blank repo as-is.
i18n.warning: Any item still reading the app dictionary directly is not installable in a blank repo. registry-builder prints a warning per such file on every build.

update.title: Updating an installed item
update.body: Run the same add command again. The CLI asks before overwriting files you have edited — read the diff before deciding, don't accept by reflex.
update.warning: Once the code is in your repo it is yours. Edit freely, but every update after that is a manual merge — that is the price of not being locked into a library.

conventions.title: Conventions
conventions.naming: Files are kebab-case and describe their purpose. An item's slug matches its directory name and its preview route param.
conventions.loc: Line limits: components and hooks ≤500, pages and layouts ≤700, config ≤1000. Split along logical boundaries, not to hit a number.
conventions.icons: Every icon goes through AppIcon by name; the library is a provider choice (currently hugeicons), swapped with one import line. shadcn primitives in ui/ keep lucide.
conventions.comments: Comments explain WHY, and never reference phase numbers or finding codes — those disappear while the code stays.
